title: Outdoor mesocosm experiments to improve understanding of risks to environmental health
protocol: Select a study site based on accessibility, availability of water supply, and potential access to power.
Consider the security of the study site due to extended experiment periods.
Ensure safe access to the site for setup, experiment, and takedown periods.
Evaluate distance from the test site to a suitable location for collecting test organisms and substrates in advance.
Conduct reconnaissance trips to find an appropriate collection site well before the experiment.
Collect biological samples from a reference area with representative diversity of organisms.
Design modular mesocosms to be transported to test sites with up to eight replicate streams arranged on treatment tables.
Arrange treatments attached to supporting wooden pallets for easy transport by forklift.
Feed river or treatment water into the polyethylene table reservoir.
Draw water from the table reservoir towards the circulation pump.
Pump water through the lower valve of the table reservoir into the March pump.
Connect one of the upper valves on the table reservoir to create system pressure.
Push water from the treatment manifold through the lower hose barbs into each stream mesocosm.
Allow water to flow through cylindrical basins in artificial streams while a motorized stirrer rotates internal paddles.
Drain overflow water onto a tray and direct it back into the table reservoir via two cylindrical funnels.
Exchange water in replicate streams every 7 minutes.
Return tray discharge to the reservoir for continued recirculation.
Completely exchange the reservoir tank's water every 1-4 hours as needed.
Transport waste water from the table or reservoir through tubing to a wastewater holding tank.
Introduce benthic substrates into each replicate stream before initiating the experiment.
Collect gravel (fine and coarse) and cobblestones from a pristine site for inoculation.
Gently hand wash cobblestones to remove attached invertebrates while maintaining preexisting periphyton community.
Create an ideal substrate layer of 2-3 cm consisting of gravel plus surface cobblestones covered with periphyton similar to the original habitat.
Use shovels for collecting fine and coarse gravel substrates.
Sieve collected gravel before transporting it to the mesocosm test site.
Transfer fine and coarse gravel to each replicate stream quickly.
Mix fine and coarse gravel gently by hand in each replicate stream.
Inoculate 32 streams with substrate.
Prepare 8-L total of >2mm to <4 mm of fine gravel for inoculation.
Prepare 24-L total of >4 mm to <9.5 mm of coarse gravel for inoculation.
Collect cobbles from the stream bottom carefully and gently hand rinse them.
Inspect collected cobbles to remove visible invertebrates with minimal disturbance.
Place cobble in a cooler maintaining original rock orientation with algae covered side facing up.
Cover cobble in water during transport to maintain periphyton community.
Place 5 cobbles in each replicate stream on top of the gravel substrate.
Allow periphyton colonization for 3-5 days, depending on ambient temperatures.
Collect benthic macroinvertebrates from a single riffle near the cobble and gravel collection site.
Ensure the collection site is upstream of the disturbance zone to maintain substrate acclimation.
Inoculate streams with collected macroinvertebrates after periphyton colonization period.
Overstock macroinvertebrates by 10-20% to account for potential mortality during handling or transport.
Collect U-nets by a team of samplers working together.
Determine the number of U-nets required based on the need for overstocking by ~10% to offset mortality during transport from river to test site.
Inoculate streams with collected macrobenthos ensuring no greater than 20% overstock compared to the riverine community.
Keep sample containers cool during transportation from collection site to mesocosm site.
Transfer collected macroinvertebrates into individual artificial streams using a randomized pattern.
Turn off motorized stirrer to help invertebrates settle into the substrate unimpeded.
Attach emergence traps or other barriers to prevent invertebrate escape after introduction.
Wait for ~2 days before initiating treatments to allow macroinvertebrates to settle.
